chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who touched his wife's private part. He said: “There is nothing upon him, and if he wishes he may wash his hand, and from a kiss one does not perform wudu (ablution).”
(58) 58 And that which indicates specifically regarding kissing—

What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about kissing: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: “There is no بأس.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem

ai.seo_question: Does touching one’s wife or kissing invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that touching one’s wife’s private part does not necessitate wudu (ablution), though washing the hand is optional. It also explicitly states that kissing does not invalidate wudu (ablution), making the report relevant to rulings of ritual purity.
